claims.harm: bundling thread safety annotations and backend changes with frontend options complicates review
claims.quote: The STDLOCK thread annotation change might make sense as a separate PR so it could be easily reviewed by people familiar with thread safety annotations
claims.settled_by_quote: Split into #34806 (internal logging api refactors) and #34809 (STDLOCK).

claims.harm: ordering and interactions between debug, trace, and exclude arguments create unnecessary RPC interface complexity
claims.quote: We have quite a bit of complexity wrt interface (documentation), implementation, and tests to deal with the interactions and ordering of these `debug`, `trace`, `exclude` options.
claims.settled_by_quote: Fair, not all breaking changes are equally breaking, and I agree we should properly weigh the impact this has on users. I'll see if I want to open a follow-up, I suspect I probably won't.

claims.harm: having three interacting flags (-debug, -trace, -debugexclude) is confusing, breaks RPC compatibility, and prevents setting trace as default while keeping specific categories at debug
claims.quote: approach NACK because having three options (`-debug`, `-trace`, `-debugexclude`) interact to control log levels is unnecessarily confusing when a single option should cover it.

support.reason: Both the new `BCLog::NO_RATE_LIMIT` and `-loglevel` changes make for a more natural and ergonomic interface for both developers and users, and the changes required are limited enough.

The new `-debug` and `-trace` startup options are a lot easier to use, and although I think the RPC interface is getting increasingly unwieldy, this seems to be the best approach minimizing breaking changes to expose the trace level there too.

result.notes: Initial record. Discussion is currently at Disputed due to ryanofsky's approach NACK proposing an alternative unified key-value -loglevel approach (#35387), while stickies-v and sedited support the PR.
